_about: The micro-kit manifest (kit 3.0, design section 3). Each micro kit owns its tools, its job kinds and its tables, and talks to the others only through the project's database (kit/tools/store.py). Every key of the growth dispatcher's TOOLS dict is in exactly ONE kit; every job kind is in exactly ONE kit; a test checks both. The pipelines at the bottom are data: adding a step to a page's line is a change here, not in code. Keys that start with an underscore are notes, never read by code. A job kind may carry use_by_days: how long its result counts (the gate's freshness rules: AI baseline, research check and review 30 days, inventory 7, link graph 8, outside facts 90); a done job of a page that is not READY yet is refreshed (a new job of the same kind) when it is within 3 days of that.

ways.ahead: ready ahead: it may run as soon as its needs are done, before anyone waits for it
ways.parallel: side by side: many of these run at the same time, limited only by their resource
ways.page: page by page: one worker (a lane) builds one page
ways.single: one at a time in the whole project: a second job of this kind waits while one is held
ways.paced: paced by a shared timer: every turn goes through `growth pace`
ways.owner: waits for the owner: no agent or machine claims it

google.what: one Google search turn every 20 to 30 s for every agent together; growth pace google (OWNER-RULES: Slow Google searches)

browser.what: a headless browser; growth.json resources.browser changes the number

port.what: a lane's own preview port; growth.json resources.port_range [first, last] changes the range

owner-preview.what: the one preview address the owner looks at; only the READY run and its move use it

shared-code.what: one writer of the shared site code (design system, shared components)

core.purpose: Bookkeeping: the project's one database, the work board, the task list, the journal, the pacer and the locks.

site.purpose: Groundwork on the whole site: the inventory, the link graph, the sitemaps, the stack, the page tracker and a page's before snapshot.

inventory.what: rebuild the site inventory (not tied to one page; a timer or the lead adds it)

link-graph.what: crawl the internal links and refresh the link graph (not tied to one page)

research.purpose: Find out what buyers and Google show before a page is planned: the page's snapshot, dossier, search figures, AI-answer baseline and the research record.

snapshot.what: the page's before snapshot (growth page_snapshot): title, headings, links, schema and its Search Console data

dossier.what: the dossier: Part 1 of the money-page playbook answered, competitors read in full
dossier._why: no google resource: the dossier reads competitor pages one by one, not Google result pages. The Google turns are in figures and ai-baseline, which are paced. use_by_days 90: the outside facts in it (vendor and competitor pages) count for 90 days (fact_sources).

figures.what: the search window: who searches, the top results, the target market's figures (growth market)

ai-baseline.what: the AI-answer baseline taken BEFORE the build: Google's AI answers, 10 or more journal runs in the primary market
ai-baseline._why: google is the only engine the kit assumes: a project's owner may forbid another one as a source. Any other engine comes only from the project's growth.json (a pacer named there, and pipeline_overrides.resource for this job).

record.what: file the research record (growth research) and the fact check the gate reads (ev.research-check counts for 30 days)

plan.purpose: Plan before building: the fact inventory, the fold plan, the plan review and the pre-flight.

fact-inventory.what: list every fact the page states, its source and the folds it sits in (each fact once in full)

fold-plan.what: growth fold_plan: all detail fields of every fold, until the plan is complete

brief.what: growth brief: the helper's brief (rules in scope, playbook steps, owner instructions); it must exist before the pre-flight (preflight needs ev.brief)

plan-review.what: the reviewer reads the fact inventory and the fold plan (about 5 minutes), BLOCKING or NIT

preflight.what: growth preflight must say PASS; it writes the page's checkpoints file

shared.purpose: Changes to code every page uses (design system, shared components) and the registry that follows them: one writer at a time.

shared-change.what: a change to shared code; holds the shared-code lock while it runs (not tied to one page)

build.purpose: Build one page in its own lane: a worktree, its own port, its own preview; then the clean-up before the final evidence.

build.what: build the page in a lane (growth lane open), gate after every fold; the job holds a preview port from the pool

cleanup.what: clear dead code and unused files BEFORE the evidence (any commit after the shots makes them stale)

check.purpose: The machine's checks: the page gate, READY, contrast, phone, technical SEO, leaks and fingerprints.

ready.what: growth ready: the full gate, 0 FAIL, on the owner's one preview address (the job holds the owner-preview lock)
ready._why: single and owner-preview together: the owner's address serves one page set at a time, so one READY job holds it; a batch of pages can still go through growth ready --batch inside that one turn. Re-checks of changed pages are new ready jobs (board.add_job).

evidence.purpose: Proof in the project: full-page shots at the rulebook's widths, the click-test of every control, page archives. Runs in a headless browser from the pool.

shots.what: screenshots at 1366 and 390 and the other rulebook widths, newer than the page's last change

click-test.what: click every control in a real browser after the page's last change

review.purpose: The independent review on a different model from the builder, and the rule that a helper runs on the model its role calls for.

review.what: the independent review of the built page: BLOCKING or NIT, accepted at 0 BLOCKING; a page sent back goes to the front of the builder's queue (ev.review counts for 30 days)

cross-check.what: the research cross-check: the built page against the dossier and concept, item by item (every search to own, buyer fear, competitor gap and fold DELIVERED, WEAK or MISSING)

cro-audit.what: the CRO audit of the built page (playbook cro-audit), only the checks the change touches

owner.purpose: Everything only the owner decides or signs: approvals, messages, the journal page, setup, health check and the guards that protect the golden rule.

owner-checkin-1.what: owner check-in 1: a few one-click questions in chat (claims, offers, old pages to merge), each with a safe default; planning goes on while they wait, the build needs the answers
owner-checkin-1._why: a project may drop it (growth.json pipeline_overrides.drop).

owner-checkin-2.what: owner check-in 2: the owner looks at the page on the one preview address (it is READY by now) and says yes or sends it back; no agent or machine claims it
owner-checkin-2._why: runner owner: a project whose owner delegated the yes can name another runner (growth.json pipeline_overrides.runner, for example agent:lead). A job for agent:lead is never given out unless the claimer asks for runner agent:lead.

release.purpose: Release one page alone after the owner's yes, get it indexed, then measure it against its baseline at day 7, 14, 28 and 56.

release.what: merge after the owner's yes and deploy, one page at a time
release._why: runner owner: the release is the lead's own act after the owner's yes (a worker agent never pushes or merges), so it is owner-side work that no agent or machine claims. The lead marks it done with `growth work done`. single keeps two releases from running at once.

measure.what: measure against the frozen baseline at day 7, 14, 28 and 56 (growth measure); the page stays at this stage until the last window is read
measure._why: the page's last stage: the machine runner marks it done only after day 56 (dates are filed by growth measure schedule).

pipelines._about: Per page type, the job kinds in order and what each needs (kinds earlier in the same line). A page added to the board gets one job per line, in this order; the page's stage is the stage of its first unfinished job. The line follows the activity map and its check: research -> plan (brief before pre-flight) -> build -> cleanup -> evidence -> review (and cross-check, CRO audit) -> ready -> owner check-in 2 -> release -> measure. A project can drop steps or change who runs one in growth.json pipeline_overrides.

money._why: The full research set: money pages carry the dossier (gate check ev.dossier, money and hub only) and the AI-answer baseline taken before the build (ev.ai-baseline, money only). The three research jobs after the snapshot do not wait for each other. The brief comes before the pre-flight (preflight needs ev.brief). Owner check-in 1 (short questions, money-page playbook step 3) is asked as soon as the record is done and sits in the line right before the build: planning goes on while the owner answers, the build needs the answers. The independent review, the research cross-check and the CRO audit come BEFORE ready (ready.py and the gate's ev.review need them) and run side by side; to run them one after the other, change their needs here. Owner check-in 2 (the prototype on the preview) is after READY: the golden rule, no address to the owner before READY.

hub._why: A hub (guide, best-software list, comparison, cluster main page) follows the cluster-redesign playbook: one researcher per page reads who searches and the top 20 results, so it gets the dossier and the search figures. No AI-answer baseline (ev.ai-baseline is money only) and no owner check-in 1 (the playbook has none; its check-in is the page on a local address). It gets the review and the research cross-check, not the CRO audit.

post._why: The lighter set for a post (new-post playbook): the snapshot, the search figures (the search it answers) and the research record with its fact check. No dossier (ev.dossier is money and hub only), no AI-answer baseline, no check-in 1 (the owner approved the topic before the job). Plan, build and checks are the same as for any page: the gate scopes them to every type. Only the independent review before READY.

core._why: A core page (contact, about, blog index) serves a known job (the money-page playbook treats the home page as a money page, so file it as money), so research is the snapshot and the research record with its fact check; no Google turns. Plan, build and checks are the same as for any page. Only the independent review before READY.
